While we anticipate the selected candidate for this position will fall towards the middle or entry point of the compensation range, the decision will be made on a case-by-case basis.

GSI Water Solutions (GSI) is seeking a skilled Hydrogeologist
who has project manager experience in California water supply issues to help manage a thriving and growing base of groundwater projects. This is an exciting opportunity to join a passionate, high-performing team of professionals making a positive impact in the water industry.

ABOUT GSI:

GSI Water Solutions is an employee-owned consulting firm specializing groundwater, environmental, and water resources with offices in Oregon, Washington, and California. At GSI, we take pride in being a company that treats its employees with respect and fairness and strives for all team members to feel they belong, have valuable insights, and can grow with us. We value work-life balance and are open to flexible work and scheduling arrangements.
As hydrogeologists, engineers, environmental scientists, and water experts, we focus on helping our clients protect our shared natural resources. We help develop and manage groundwater resources and ensure the long-term sustainability and reliability of this invaluable resource.

Learn more on our website: https://gsiwatersolutions.com/

ABOUT OUR HYDROGEOLOGISTS:

Our Hydrogeologists, Mid-Career
play a crucial role by combining technical expertise with strong managerial and leadership skills. They ensure the successful completion of projects through complex analyses, meticulous project management, insightful interpretation of data, and report writing. They typically manage smaller projects (or aspects of larger projects) with the potential to take on more complex projects as experience is acquired. Their ability to mentor junior staff and cultivate client relationships underscores their pivotal contribution to our continued growth and success in the industry.

IN THIS ROLE YOU WILL:

Complete complex analyses and calculations.
Manage and organize field programs and conduct technical briefings to field staff.
Perform interpretation of subsurface data.
Generate complete proposals and technical reports.
Participate in technical review of project work and reports.
Develop project budgets and scopes for review by senior-level project manager.
Participate in contract review.
Develop and maintain client contact before and after completion of job.
Participate in marketing activities.
Mentor entry-level and other mid-career staff to develop skills in fieldwork, data interpretation and project management.

REQUIRED EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:

Any combination of experience and training that would likely provide the required knowledge and abilities is qualifying. Typical ways to obtain the required knowledge and abilities include:
Master’s degree from an accredited college or university in hydrogeology or geology plus a minimum of 6 years of professional experience;
-OR- a Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university in hydrogeology or geology plus a minimum of 8 years of professional experience.
-AND- 2 years experience in managing projects.

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, AND REGISTRATIONS:

Professional geologist or certified hydrogeologist license within the state that work will be performed is preferred.
Current and valid driver's license and clean driving record.

VALUED EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:

Experience in water resources planning, water supply development, and/or groundwater management in California.
Advanced coursework in hydrogeology.
Experience in groundwater supply, municipal production well design, construction, and testing, environmental groundwater characterization, and/or water resource management projects, including preparation of technical reports and proposals and budgets.
Thorough knowledge of groundwater flow and well hydraulics.

SUCCESS FACTORS:

An understanding of the technical complexities of groundwater management issues in California.
Proficient in all phases of business development activities.
Excellent technical skills with the ability to organize and manage work efforts of various types.
Excellent verbal and written communication, organizational, and report-writing skills.
Ability to work independently and in teams.
A self-starter with an entrepreneurial character.
Emotional intelligence and humility.
Appreciation for diversity.
Service and action-oriented.

BENEFITS:

Flexible/hybrid work schedules
401k with employer match, up to 4%
Potential for annual bonus based on company performance.
Employee-Owned company through Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP)
Highly competitive medical, dental, vision insurance plans for employees and their families with alternative care coverage included in medical plans.
Access to medical and dependent-care flexible spending accounts
Employer paid short-term disability, long-term disability, and life insurance.
5 weeks of paid time off annually (pro-rated the first year based on start date)
Paid time off for certification and licensing exams
Paid attendance at professional conferences in support of career development
Paid memberships in professional organizations
Reimbursement for professional registrations and renewals
Cell phone stipend to assist with the cost of using a personal cell phone for business purposes
Discounts on Carhartt and Danner clothing and footwear

TO APPLY:

Please submit your resume
along with a cover letter
outlining your interest in the position and how your experience aligns with the role.

We encourage candidates to apply even if they do not meet every qualification listed. We value potential, transferable skills, and a willingness to learn just as much as direct experience. Research shows that many qualified candidates, particularly those from historically marginalized communities, hesitate to apply unless they meet 100% of the criteria. We’re interested in the whole person, not just a checklist.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS AND WORK ENVIRONMENT:

The physical demands and work environment described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
The work performed is conducted primarily in a professional office environment and requires the use of standard office equipment such as computers, phones, and copiers.
While performing the duties of the job, you will frequently be required to sit, talk, and hear. Visual acuity sufficient to view documents and computer screens, with or without correction, is required. Occasionally required to reach with hands and arms, climb short distances, balance and stoop, kneel and crouch.
Fieldwork activities may involve lifting and carrying equipment weighing up to 50 pounds, bending, stooping, and walking over uneven terrain.
Fieldwork activities may include exposure to various environmental conditions, including but not limited to: inclement weather, extreme temperatures, rugged terrain, and/or potential exposure to hazardous materials. Personal protective equipment (PPE) will be provided and required for field activities to ensure safety and compliance with OSHA standards.
Travel to project sites, client meetings, and regulatory agencies as needed. Travel frequency will vary depending on project locations and requirements but, in general, will comprise approximately 30-50% of work time. Project areas are generally local, or within an approximately a two to three-hour drive.

Integration meets Innovation
At Celigo, we believe integration should empower — not exhaust — innovation. As a modern Integration and Automation Platform (iPaaS), we’re on a mission to simplify how companies integrate, automate, and optimize processes. Powered by game-changing technology like runtime AI and prebuilt, mission-critical integrations, Celigo is redefining how businesses connect their world.
As a Product Data Analyst  you will play a critical role in Celigo’s success and help execute quantitative research tasks throughout the product development lifecycle to ensure that we’re solving the right problems and providing the right solutions for our target audiences and users. The Product Data Analyst  works strategically, proactively, and collaboratively to inform and influence product roadmaps and business goals.

We are seeking a Product Data Analyst to partner closely with UX Research, Product Management, Design, Content, Engineering, and Customer-facing teams to uncover actionable insights from behavioral and product usage data.
This role sits within the UX Research team in the Product organization and will partner closely with  product managers and designers to uncover actionable insights from behavioral and product usage data.

Partner with members of the Design, Content, and Product Management teams to uncover what they need to learn from quantitative data sources (and why) and then identify, pull, and analyze the necessary data to provide them with actionable insights rather than tables of raw data.
Collaborate closely with designers to define, track, and report on metrics that demonstrate the business and user impact of their work as well as craft measurable hypotheses for new and existing features.
Be curious, proactively analyze data, and surface insights that influence product strategy, roadmap decisions, and customer experience improvements.
Help train peers to effectively utilize user research findings and usage metrics to guide and improve design decisions.
Support research operations tasks such as pulling recruitment lists and answering ad-hoc data questions.
Build and maintain dashboards and self-serve reporting frameworks that empower cross-functional teams.
Translate ambiguous business questions into structured analyses and clear recommendations.
Identify leading indicators of engagement, activation, retention, and expansion.

Ability to analyze and synthesize data, and guide product managers, designers, and engineers on how to act on the findings.

4–6+ years of experience in Product Analytics or a similar role supporting B2B SaaS or enterprise software products.

Experience working with product analytics tools (e.g., Pendo, Google Analytics) and BI tools (e.g., Sigma).

Funded by UGS base funding supplemented by Federal projects at multiple scales including projects for NPS, BLM, USFS, and Statemap. The incumbent will be responsible for overseeing paleontological field work and the preparation lab for a variety of paleontological projects with a focus on resource inventory, salvage, and research in support of understanding Utah’s geological history and stratigraphic framework. Job Description

The Geologic Mapping and Paleontology Program of the Utah Geological Survey (UGS) is seeking a full time permanent Preparator – Field Paleontologist. This is a unique opportunity to build a career focused on Field Paleontology in Utah. This position will be focused on fulfilling Utah paleontology regulation regarding the documentation, preservation, and promotion of Utah’s vast paleontological resource. Funded by UGS base funding supplemented by Federal projects at multiple scales including projects for NPS, BLM, USFS, and Statemap. The incumbent will be responsible for overseeing paleontological field work and the preparation lab for a variety of paleontological projects with a focus on resource inventory, salvage, and research in support of understanding Utah’s geological history and stratigraphic framework. Maintenance of Utah’s ever growing Paleontological Locality Database is a critical part of the program and with 25,000 records it is unrivaled anywhere.

Key Responsibilities

Key responsibilities and day to day responsibilities of this position:

Oversee fossil preparation in UGS preparation lab by insuring equipment is operational, preparing significant fossils, overseeing volunteers, organizing the transfer of prepared specimens into appropriate repositories. Supervise paleontological field work by overseeing base camp operations, excavations, volunteers, collecting field data, and creating digital paleontological locality files.
Perform geologic field work that includes putting paleontological field data into geological context stratigraphically and geographically.
Prepare paleontological permit applications, supporting materials, and final reports for federal and state agencies as needed working with State Paleontologist.
Review paleontological reports and publications for UGS, external scientists, and students. Address review comments and complete reports on time for contract deliverables, provide timely reviews of geologic publications in collaboration with other UGS staff and outside geoscientists.
Work closely with the State Paleontologist to address issues related to paleontological resource management on public lands.
Develop paleontological and geologic expertise for Utah and share this expertise via conferences, publishing, and public interaction.
Collaborate with other Utah Geological Survey staff and external scientists investigating the geological heritage of Utah.

Qualifications

Minimum or "day-one" qualifications:

B.S. in Geology or Biology (Paleontology) required; M.S. or Ph.D. in Geology or Biology (Paleontology) is preferred.
May underfill based on candidates experience level.
Project Geologist - must be licensed as a geologist in the state of Utah.
Geologist - doesn't require licensure, but the incumbent is generally working toward becoming licensed.

Must have experience in vertebrate fossil preparation and field excavation.
Need to be able to assure personal safety in a variety of remote wilderness and urban settings.

Preferred Or Trainable/on-the-job Qualifications

new_jobs.title: Remote Virtual Project Coordinator Full-Time / Part-Time
new_jobs.description:
We are seeking a highly organized and detail-oriented Remote Virtual Project Coordinator
to support project planning, coordination, communication, and execution across multiple teams. In this work-from-home role, you will assist project managers by tracking project activities, maintaining documentation, coordinating schedules, monitoring deadlines, and ensuring projects stay on track. The ideal candidate is proactive, organized, and skilled at managing multiple priorities in a virtual environment.

Responsibilities

Assist with planning, coordinating, and monitoring projects from initiation through completion.
Maintain project schedules, timelines, milestones, and task assignments.
Track project progress and follow up with team members on deliverables.
Coordinate virtual meetings, prepare agendas, document meeting notes, and track action items.
Maintain project documentation, reports, status updates, and project files.
Communicate project updates, deadlines, and changes to internal teams and stakeholders.
Support project managers with administrative and operational tasks.
Monitor project risks, issues, and dependencies and escalate concerns when necessary.
Manage project management tools and update task statuses regularly.
Prepare project reports, dashboards, and performance summaries.
Coordinate communication between departments, vendors, and external partners.
Assist with resource tracking, scheduling, and workflow organization.
Ensure project activities follow company policies, procedures, and quality standards.
Identify opportunities to improve project processes and team efficiency.
Perform additional project support duties as assigned.

Required Qualifications

Previous experience in project coordination, administrative support, operations, or a similar role preferred.
Strong organizational and time management skills.
Excellent written and verbal communication abilities.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook) and Google Workspace.
Experience with project management tools such as Asana, Trello, Monday.com, Jira, ClickUp, or Microsoft Project is preferred.
Ability to manage multiple tasks, deadlines, and priorities effectively.
Strong attention to detail and problem-solving skills.
Ability to work independently and collaborate effectively in a remote environment.
Reliable internet connection and a dedicated home workspace.

new_jobs.title: Program Coordinator (TOP Clubhouse)
new_jobs.description:
Organization Overview:
The Goddard Riverside Community Center (Goddard Riverside) and the Stanley M. Isaacs Neighborhood Center (Isaacs Center) are well-established Manhattan community-based agencies that support services to approximately 30,000 New Yorkers. We are two of New York City’s leading human services organizations meeting the needs of children, youth and families, homeless individuals, and older adults through-out Manhattan and New York City. We work every day for a fair and just society where all people have the opportunity to make choices that lead to better lives for themselves and their families.

Program Description:
TOP Clubhouse is an evidence-based model that empowers individuals with a mental illness to focus on their own personal recovery goals through a holistic paradigm that integrates education, employment, and socialization. This unique model allows members to grow more confident in a range of tasks by working side-by-side with staff and other members. This model challenges the stigma around the client versus clinician relationship which is the more traditional model in many day programs. The clubhouse model considers staff and members as colleagues and every individual has unique talents and strengths that enhance our community.

Purpose of Position:
TOP Clubhouse is seeking a dynamic individual who will work with the Program Director to ensure quality and integrity of the program. This person must be innovative, creative, proactive, and detailed-oriented, with excellent organizational skills that will promote a positive work environment. The Program Coordinator is responsible for integrating services, staff support, and assuming overall leadership of TOP Clubhouse in the absence of the Program Director.

Schedule:
Monday through Friday 9:00 am to 5:00 pm. Some weekends and evenings required.

Salary Range:
$52,020 - $58,000
